result.topic_en: The page completes a criterion for continuity via fundamental sequences, then notes research problems on algebraic numbers satisfying linear differential equations, on proving the rationality of Bernoulli numbers from Riemann's zeta integral, and on proving Wiener's assertion about the special Pascal theorem.

items.english: All such fundamental sequences then necessarily represent one and the same value, as one can easily show, and this value is $=f(a)$.

items.english: Which algebraic numbers satisfy linear differential equations of 1st and 2nd order? In my sense, i.e. the sense determined by congruences.

items.english: For the linear differential equations of 2nd order, see whether the quotient of the integrals can be inverted and then yields the values of elliptic functions for singular moduli, or something similar.

items.english: From Riemann's integral for the zeta functions, try to show that the Bernoulli numbers are rational, in order thereby perhaps to obtain a better estimate for the value of the largest number contained in it.
